import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate Total Spending by summing all 'Mnt' columns
spending_cols = [
    'MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts',
    'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds'
]
df['Total_Spending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Drop rows where Income is NaN, as income is crucial for this visualization
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Filter out extreme income outliers for better visualization clarity
# Incomes above 150,000 are very few and can compress the main data points.
df_filtered = df[df['Income'] < 150000].copy()

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Education',
    palette='viridis', # 'viridis' is a perceptually uniform colormap
    alpha=0.7,         # Transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    s=60,              # Size of the points
    edgecolor='w',     # White edge around points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5      # Line width of the point edge
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Total Customer Spending vs. Income, Grouped by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Amount Spent on Products', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to not overlap with data points
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', frameon=True)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels and legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
